subject: Close date drift — postmortem and mitigation commitments
messages:
From: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@acme.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, Jun 28 2027 12:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Heads-up: internal timeline slip on evaluation — potential close push

Marissa,

Quick note from our side: during this morning's internal review we pushed the product sign-off week out by two weeks. The evaluation team flagged a dependency on a privacy review that wasn't in their original plan. That moves our close target from Jul 15 -> Jul 29 unless we accelerate some items.

Immediate asks: can Redwood provide an updated MAP with hard dates for the evaluation checkpoints and a short remediation plan we can show leadership? Also — any flexibility on a temporary dev token or test environment access to help speed validation?

I'll loop Sarah from Procurement if we need to re-open contract dates.

—Tom
Tom Hargrove
Dir, IT Integrations | Acme Corp

Attachment: none (referenced internal notes)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 28 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: internal timeline slip on evaluation — potential close push

Tom — thanks for the heads-up and sorry to hear about the privacy gating item. We can move fast on our side. Action items from Redwood: 

- I attached a revised MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) that pins concrete owners and milestone dates; key changes are the evaluation sign-off window (now split into two incremental checkpoints) and a contingency column with fallbacks.
- We can provision a short-lived dev token + isolated test instance for your evaluation team within 24 hours. Jonas will coordinate the access details.
- Ben will draft a 1-page remediation plan you can present to your CIO that calls out where Redwood can absorb acceptance testing time and where we need your SMEs.

Two asks from you: please confirm the privacy review owner and a hard date for when their approval will be available (we modeled Jul 12 in the MAP but can adjust). Second, confirm whether Procurement needs a contract amendment for a potential two-week extension or if you prefer handling as a minor SOW addendum.

I believe we can keep the close in the July window if we get the privacy sign-off and the dev token is used to parallelize functional validation. If not, we'll prepare a rebaseline and escalate.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 115KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, Jun 29 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: internal timeline slip on evaluation — potential close push

Following up with a short remediation draft (summary here) that I'll attach as a formal PDF this morning. Core items: 

1) Parallel verify: Redwood will run the first acceptance test in our infra 48h after your dev token activation and share logs. Target: reduce your on-prem validation from 5 days to 2 by validating integration points on Redwood-side.
2) Contingency runbook: if privacy sign-off misses Jul 12, we propose a staged acceptance that decouples functional pass from privacy stamp for sandbox testing only. Production release gated on final approval.
3) Timeline rebaseline: fallback close date = Jul 29; interim checkpoints on Jul 9 (functional smoke), Jul 16 (integration), Jul 23 (final sign-off prep).

I've attached evaluation_plan_notes.pdf and a draft postmortem docx that describes root causes we observed across similar deals (people handoffs + missing owner for privacy scope).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: evaluation_plan_notes.pdf (4 pages, 80KB); close_drift_postmortem.docx (22KB)

Subject: Escalation: close-date contingency confirmation and credit request

Tom / Sarah — quick update after Ben and Jonas's work this morning. Summary of where we stand and what we need by EOD Friday (Jul 2):

- Redwood commits to provisioning the dev token and test instance by Tue Jun 29 (completed). Jonas will deliver access notes and a short validation checklist.
- Privacy owner confirmation required: you indicated Jul 12 — please reply with the approver name and the expected sign-off artifact (email or ticket id). If we do not receive confirmation by EOD Fri (Jul 2), we will assume the privacy approval is at risk and move the fallback close to Jul 29.
- Because this is a timeline-driven commercial impact, I've cc'd Lauren (Sales Director) to approve a one-time commercial credit if the close slips past Jul 22 due to Acme-driven gating. Lauren — please confirm whether we can offer a credit covering 50% of one month's committed usage as a goodwill gesture if the final production cutover misses Jul 22.

If Acme confirms the privacy owner and provides the artifact by Friday, Redwood will keep the original close window and run the parallel verification plan to compress your validation runway. If not, we'll issue a short amendment to formalize the Jul 29 fallback and the checkpoints.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated), evaluation_plan_notes.pdf, close_drift_postmortem.docx

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmation.

Marissa Cole
